items.title: Dalton Richards Interview, 1961-03-16
items.q: And, uh, we had the same group with Albert French, Howard Davis, Alvin Alcon, and, uh, Sidney Montaguey on the drums.

ctx.x: They just paid you a flat sum, you didn't get tips or anything at the party?

No, no tips. No tips. Now, when we would play some of, for some of the white people, you'd make tips. Sometimes a fellow would actually play Satan numbers, they wanted all the old numbers that you could think of, like after the ball was over, down by the old mill stream, so they could get a, what you would call a drunken chord group around the piano and all the things. And later on, I found out that that did benefit me by me knowing those numbers, because one time I played for, or some people, I forget who they…

Yeah, I'm trying to think, who's Eugene Boyd? I can't remember. He's a tennis saxophone player. Tennis sax. I knew, I didn't know him, but I was George Boyd. George Boyd, they called him George Boyd. The clarinet player way back. But, uh, I know a lot of people worked with him. I didn't know him personally.
